topic: Clinically important drug-drug interactions during tuberculosis treatment

rifamycin_induction.clinical_effect: Can markedly lower exposure to many concomitant medicines; magnitude varies by rifamycin and interacting drug.

linezolid_MAO.clinical_effect: Potential serotonin toxicity with serotonergic medicines; absolute risk appears low in observational cohorts but requires vigilance.

additive_QT.clinical_effect: Additive QT prolongation; evaluate ECG, electrolytes and other QT-prolonging medicines.

high_priority_pairs.risk: Reduced hormone exposure / possible reduced contraceptive effectiveness
Major change/reduction in anticoagulant exposure; management depends on specific agent
Reduced dolutegravir exposure; WHO specifies regimen adjustment
Potential loss of efficacy of concomitant therapy
Potential serotonin toxicity; rare but clinically important

chatbot_rules: Never answer 'yes, safe' or 'no, contraindicated' from drug names alone when a guideline-specific adjustment may exist.
Ask/retrieve the exact concomitant medicine, dose, indication, TB regimen, renal/hepatic context and relevant monitoring.
Prioritize WHO/CDC guideline instructions over a general interaction database when TB-specific guidance exists.
For rifamycins, distinguish rifampicin, rifapentine and rifabutin; their interaction magnitude is not interchangeable.
Do not advise independent changes to anticoagulants, antiretrovirals, anticonvulsants, transplant medicines or hormonal contraception.
For linezolid plus serotonergic agents, distinguish theoretical interaction from actual symptoms of serotonin toxicity.
